change: Deployed the vectorized arch-v2 SCReLU head (commit 9367cd6) and S3 futility pruning (commit 2f5c16e) to the Threadripper production box, which had been pinned at 0ebaffe since the campaign_v6 mint and was therefore running the pre-vectorization scalar head.
why: The campaign_v6 gate was measuring the v2 h1024 learner at 0.253x the NPS of the v1 h64 incumbent (432,958 vs 1,709,562 in the cycle-46 gate match), conceding ~1.3 plies of search depth. The 2x head vectorization had been committed locally on 2026-08-08 but never reached the box.

build_verification.note: Deterministic acceptance signature matches the documented post-S3 baseline exactly, proving the box rebuilt the new source rather than reusing a stale binary.
build_verification.arch_v2_parity_tests: 4 passed, 0 failed (index fixture, incremental==full, SCReLU==reference, Python-exported gold model integer-exact) - confirms the i32 chunked head is integer-identical on AVX2, not only on NEON.

measurement.method: scripts/experiments/nps_bench.py, interactive UCI, Threads 1, Hash 256, blend 100, go movetime 3000, 6 positions x 2 interleaved rounds, fresh engine per round.

cross_platform_comparison.note: AVX2 realizes slightly more of the vectorization than NEON, as the evidence file for 9367cd6 anticipated when it asked for a re-measurement on this hardware.

caveat: The nps_bench conditions (blend 100, movetime 3000, fixed position set) are not the gate conditions (gate blend/time control and book openings), so the gate ratio will not land exactly at 0.554. The kernel speedup itself is confirmed; the gate effect must be read from the next cycle's gate_compare_same_blend.json.
outcome: The v2 gate handicap drops from roughly a 2-ply deficit to roughly half a ply. Residual handicap is on the order of 30-60 Elo rather than 100-150.
